note: From the OpenStreetMap export (tools/osm-to-kit.mjs and the corridor's tracks, 8 October 2026), at real scale across the line like the tracks: island 3/4 between platform 4 (the stopper to Manchester, turning round) and platform 3, with bay 3a cut into its north end; island 1/2 beyond the fast lines, with platform 1 on its far side where the Hazel Grove line turns round, so passengers changing between the two walk through the subway; the platform 0 bay outside it; the carriage sidings and the Edgeley lines to the west; No.1 signal box on the end of island 3/4 and No.2 between the lines at the north end. Positive v is east (Station Road, Grand Central). The island buildings are set back from platform 4's edge to leave room to wait, from memory. Photos: platform 4's long canopy on slim columns (red until about 2020, navy with white bands since: geograph 5195033 David Dixon 2016 against 8388762 and 8414073 DS Pugh 2026, 7798745 JThomas 2024), a long brick retaining wall along the Station Road approach, and the Network Rail depot south of the station. The Station Road entrance (geograph 8196049 Stephen Craven 2025, 8414067 DS Pugh 2026, 6148242 HelenK 2019, 5113253 2016) is a glass drum, round towards the plaza, about 25 m across and 7.5 m high under a thin flat roof slab that overhangs and follows the curve, set against the brick building (the `drum` part); its depth the photos can't show, so it's drawn 9 m out. There is no footbridge: the subway is the way across. It starts as a halt: a strip of island 3/4 along platform 4 with a shelter and lamps. The subway, then platform 3 (the rest of the island, and room for a second train to turn), the booking hall (the island's buildings and the Station Road building), and platforms 0, 1 and 2 build it up; the sidings, signal boxes, depot, walls and car park are scenery. Departure boards on platforms 4, 3 and 1 and over the Station Road entrance; cars on the roof deck of the multi-storey car park, and Sheffield stands by the Station Road entrance (from memory) with the booking hall. Re-laid 13 October 2026 from OpenStreetMap's tracks so the layout keeps its rule (docs/DESIGN.md, Where the tracks run): the station narrowed towards its real width at the platforms' north end (island 3/4 now 19.5 m across, island 1/2 14 m, the Station Road side 29.5 m nearer the line), the platforms ending at u = 120 so the throat fits before and on the viaduct's first spans, bay 3a joining the down fast, platform 0 joining the up slow, the Edgeley lines joining the down slow before the viaduct, and the carriage sidings leaving a lead at turnouts rather than fanning straight in; No.2 box between the up fast and up slow at the throat. Which side Station Road is (13 October 2026, OpenStreetMap's API): two roads carry the name. The main one, to the entrance and Stockport Exchange, runs on the east (+v) side, where the NCP Stockport Exchange multi-storey (1,000 spaces, way 459252093, u -115 to -20, v 90 to 206) stands as the kit's multi-storey does; the other is a cobbled lane on the west side (way 41772029, u -174 to -1, v -43 to -19) with 20-minute parking along it, the 'Station Road car park' of geograph 8413983. So the kit's east side stands. Across the line at real scale since 13 October 2026 (it was 1.25 times).

Stockport Interchange: the bus station between Wellington Road (the A6) and the viaduct, centred about 53.40889, -2.16306 (Wikipedia, Stockport Interchange, which gives 18 stands, opened 17 March 2024, under Viaduct Park, a 2-acre (0.8 ha) roof garden, beside a 17-storey block of flats, with a link to Station Road). Placed at its real distance from the station; six of the stands drawn, along its viaduct side; the hall about 105 by 50 m and 9 m to the park, the flats, the helix ramp and the Station Road link left out; sizes from memory.
